name: Scottish Cullen Skink
description: Cullen skink has a genuinely fascinating real history behind its name - 'skink' is old Scots for a broth traditionally made from beef shin, but when the fishing village of Cullen fell on hard economic times in the 19th century, expensive beef was swapped for the plentiful smoked haddock its coast was already known for, and a new dish was born. Real technique gently poaches the fish in milk and water rather than boiling it hard, which keeps it tender.

ingredients_full.note: tsp, for a hint of smokiness

ingredients.note: tsp, for a hint of smokiness

steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the butter, 4-5 minutes, without letting it brown.
Add the potato, milk, 1 cup water, and bay leaf, and simmer 12-15 minutes until the potato is nearly tender.
Season the fish with the paprika, add to the pot, and gently poach 8-10 minutes until just cooked through, keeping the liquid at a gentle simmer, never a hard boil.
Mash some of the potato against the side of the pot to thicken the soup slightly.

name: Scottish Haggis-Style Skillet
description: Real haggis is traditionally made from sheep's offal (liver, heart, and lungs) mixed with oats and suet, and cooked stuffed inside a real stomach casing - organ meats and a stomach casing aren't practical or reliably available ingredients here, so this version honestly approximates only the flavor profile using ground beef, oats, and the dish's real warming spice blend, in a skillet rather than a true haggis.
steps_detailed: Toast the oats in a dry pan over medium heat, 3-4 minutes, until golden and fragrant.
Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the toasted oats, black pepper, and nutmeg, being generous with the pepper, and cook 3-4 minutes more until well combined.

name: Scottish Neeps and Tatties
description: Neeps and tatties, mashed turnip and mashed potato served separately side by side, is the real, traditional accompaniment to haggis.

ingredients_full.note: boiled and mashed, standing in for turnip/swede

steps_detailed: Boil the potato and squash separately until each is completely tender, 15-18 minutes.
Mash each separately with half the butter, keeping them as two distinct sides rather than combining.

name: Scottish Cranachan
description: Cranachan, a real dessert of whipped cream, toasted oats, honey, and berries, real technique toasts the oats until genuinely golden and fragrant first, which is what gives the dish its real nutty crunch against the soft cream.
steps_detailed: Toast the oats in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, 3-4 minutes, until deeply golden and fragrant.
Whip the cream to soft peaks.
Layer the whipped cream, toasted oats, honey, and berries in a glass, alternating layers.

name: Scottish Shortbread
description: Shortbread, a real, simple butter cookie, is one of Scotland's most iconic exports, real technique using a genuinely high proportion of butter and working the dough as little as possible for a real tender, crumbly texture.
steps_detailed: Cream the butter and sugar briefly, then work in the flour just until it comes together - real technique avoids overworking the dough, which keeps it tender.
Press into a small pan and prick all over with a fork.
Bake at 325F (165C) for 25-28 minutes until pale golden, not deeply browned.

name: Scottish Grilled Salmon
description: Grilled salmon, seasoned simply with dill and lemon, reflects Scotland's real, celebrated salmon fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the salmon with the dill and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
